strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with intermediate scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 16 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially, each preceded by local per-shard scaling (multiply by a[r]/W) and followed by local normalization (divide by a[r]). Total dispatch count is 16 all-reduces plus O(16) local elementwise ops. Trades off simplicity and correctness for high latency due to sequential dependencies.

strategies.name: Fused buffer preparation with batched all-reduce
strategies.desc: Pre-compute all 16 buffer transformations locally (scale operations) and store them, then pipeline the all-reduce calls to maximize network utilization. Uses async dispatch if available to overlap computation of buffer[i+1] with communication of buffer[i]. Dispatch count remains 16 all-reduces but reduces bubble time between consecutive collectives through better scheduling.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter and all-gather decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair, allowing local computation on reduced chunks between the two phases. For 16 iterations, this yields 32 collectives but enables better overlap of smaller payloads (W*256/W per reduce-scatter) with local scaling operations. Trades collective count for reduced per-collective payload and potential compute-communication overlap.

strategies.name: Hierarchical reduction with node-local aggregation
strategies.desc: Exploit multi-node topology by performing intra-node reductions first (lower latency), then inter-node aggregation, then broadcast back. Each of 16 iterations uses 3 collectives (intra-node all-reduce, inter-node all-reduce on representatives, intra-node broadcast) for 48 total dispatches. Optimizes for network topology at cost of increased collective count.

strategies.name: Vectorized buffer transformation with minimal clones
strategies.desc:
Eliminate per-iteration clone() calls by reusing two ping-pong buffers alternately across iterations. Vectorize the scaling operations across all shards using tensor views rather than explicit loops. Maintains 16 all-reduces but reduces memory allocation overhead and improves cache locality through buffer reuse. Same algorithmic structure but better memory efficiency.
